newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE's Al-Rostamani launches industrial estate.
newsitem.headline: UAE's Al-Rostamani launches industrial estate.

text.p: Al-Rostamani Real Estate Co, a unit of Dubai's $1.5 billion al-Rostamani family conglomerate, said on Tuesday it had launched the first private industrial estate in the United Arab Emirates.

The project in Sharjah -- one of seven emirates in the UAE -- cost 150 million dirhams ($41 million) excluding the cost of land, Abdul Wahed al-Rostamani, RRE's managing director, said at a news conference.
He said the project extending over more than 270 hectares (660 acres) would offer 650 fully developed industrial plots by the first quarter of 1997.
"One hundred and ninety plots are ready now and we are working on the remaining plots," said Azmi Oran, RRE general manager.
Al-Rostamani said the choice of Sharjah was due to the encouraging "pro-industry" policy adopted by the emirate.
Unlike other emirates, Sharjah, home to 46 percent of the UAE's industrial concerns, allows 100 percent land ownership to Arab Nationals.
Factories in Sharjah are privately owned.
Elsewhere in the UAE, the manufacturing landscape is dominated by big government or quasi-state concerns.
Al-Rostamani said the Sharjah government would look on a case-by-case basis at granting facilities and full ownership to non-Arab industrialists.
